title: Lightweight edge translation shim for OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Customers integrating Redwood with existing clients built for the OpenAI Chat Completions (OA-CC) API expect identical request/response semantics for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. Current broad compatibility efforts are heavyweight and embed protocol translation in the central gateway. This ticket proposes a lightweight edge translation shim that can be deployed at the ingress (hosted or Dedicated edge) to normalize OA-CC requests into Redwood internal request shapes and to rehydrate Redwood responses back to OA-CC clients with minimal fidelity loss.
acceptance_criteria: 1) OA-CC request payloads (messages, system prompts, temperature/top_p, function schemas) accepted by shim are transformed to Redwood request model with consistent deterministic mapping. 2) Streaming mode: shim replays token deltas to OA-CC SSE clients (data: event chunks) preserving order, tool-call frames, and stream-level stop tokens. 3) Function/tool calling flows: shim supports two modes — full function resolution (Redwood invokes 3rd-party tools and returns final assistant message) and passthrough function-call events (emit partial function call frames while model streams). 4) Structured outputs: shim enforces JSON schema constraints when OA-CC 'response_format' meta is present; on validation failures emit OA-CC style error object and attempt best-effort sanitized structured output. 5) Error mapping: Redwood internal error codes map predictably to OA-CC HTTP status / error messages. 6) End-to-end tests (unit + integration) covering streaming, non-streaming, function-call, and malformed payloads. 7) Performance overhead at edge < 3% p50 latency and not exceed 5% CPU on typical ingress instance.
technical_approach: High level: implement a pluggable ingress middleware service (Go) that sits between public OA-CC endpoints and internal Redwood routing. Responsibilities: parse OA-CC request shapes (messages[], model alias, functions[] with JSON schemas), normalize into Redwood internal request (compact prompt envelope, function metadata, streaming flags), and add translation metadata for later back-translation. Streaming: subscribe to internal response stream and translate token deltas into OA-CC SSE frames; maintain stream windowing so partial function invocation tokens are emitted as function_call objects per OA-CC semantics. Tool / function calling: support two integration strategies selectable per-tenant via a capability flag: (A) resolve-at-edge: edge calls out to registered tool adapters (HTTP hooks) when the model emits function_call and returns invocation result to model agent before concluding — reduces round trips to downstream services; (B) brokered-flow: emit function_call to OA-CC client or downstream system and expect an external caller to provide function_result via a follow-up event. Structured output: run a light JSON-schema validator on streaming checkpoints (every N tokens or on candidate closing) and attempt minimal-normalization (trim trailing commas, wrap bare text into {"text": ...}) before emitting final assistant message. Telemetry: add mapping-layer telemetry tags (orig_request_id, mapping_version, translation_time_ms) and propagate trace headers for distributed tracing.
implementation_notes: - Keep the shim stateless for primary request path; store ephemeral mapping state in an in-memory per-request context with TTL. - Provide an opt-in compatibility header X-Redwood-Compat: openai_chat_completions=v1 to avoid surprising existing Redwood-only clients. - Maintain idempotency by canonicalizing OA-CC client message IDs to internal request IDs. - For streaming, handle early client disconnects: if OA-CC client disconnects, send a cancel to internal runtime and log session-level diagnostics. - Provide a feature flag to fallback to 'compatibility-dropin' which will rewrite function_call outputs into simple assistant messages if downstream tool adapters aren't available. - Document explicit behavior differences in the compatibility README and public changelog.
risks_and_mitigation: 1) Fidelity loss for edge cases (complex function schemas with circular refs): mitigate by returning best-effort error and link to detailed compatibility guide. 2) Performance regression under heavy streaming: add circuit breaker to fall back to non-streaming compatibility mode for affected tenants. 3) Security: function schema could carry sensitive inline examples — the shim strips any explicit secrets from outbound tool invocation payloads and requires tool adapters to have KMS-backed credentials. 4) Ambiguous partial function-call semantics across OA-CC clients: provide an explicit mapping doc and a compatibility test suite customers can run.
test_plan: - Unit tests for mapping rules (field-by-field) covering top_p/temperature, role normalization, attachments, and functions[]. - Integration test harness that spins up the shim, a Redwood runtime mock, and an OA-CC client emulator to assert streaming frames order and toolcall frame semantics. - Fuzz tests with malformed schemas and large function lists. - Performance benchmark scenario: 100 concurrent streaming sessions, median message length 128 tokens, measure p50/p95 shim CPU and added latency. - Canary rollout to small set of tenants via feature flag and monitor error rate and latency in Console dashboards.
